title: Unquoted variable (or $( )) expansion used as a word instead of an argument
purpose: Prevent word-splitting and globbing from turning a single value that is meant to be one argument into several, corrupting every later argument wherever the value holds spaces, globs or is empty.
trigger: A positional/argument position expands a variable, parameter or $( ) substitution without double quotes (for example $name, $@ as a lone command argument, or ${arr[*]} where each element must be a separate word), so Bash splits the result on whitespace or expands globs.
correct: Double-quote the expansion: "$name", "${arr[@]}". Use an unquoted expansion only in the specific, deliberate cases where you want splitting, and make that intent obvious.
evidence_note: Grounded in queuebash.sh and bin/queue-* which spread expansions and compose commands as quoted arrays so spaces/newlines survive.
return_semantics: A reference rule page; shown for LLM author guidance, not executed by rules check.
